# bb tag

Create, list, view and delete tags

4 commands.

[`bb tag create`](#bb-tag-create)
:   Create repository tag

[`bb tag delete`](#bb-tag-delete)
:   Delete repository tag

[`bb tag list`](#bb-tag-list)
:   List repository tags

[`bb tag view`](#bb-tag-view)
:   View repository tag

## `bb tag create`

Create repository tag

```text
bb tag create <name> [flags]
```

```bash
# Tag the tip of main
bb tag create v1.2.0 --start-point main --repo PROJ/repo

# An annotated tag on a commit
bb tag create v1.2.0 --start-point a1b2c3d --message "Release 1.2.0" --repo PROJ/repo
```

`--message string`
:   Optional annotated tag message

`--start-point string`
:   Commit ID or ref to tag

Inherited from [`bb tag`](#bb-tag):

`--filter string`
:   Filter text for tag names

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Checks your permission and the current state this depends on, without changing anything (preconditions-checked)

<details class="note" data-search-exclude>
<summary>Output with <code>--json</code>, where <code>?</code> marks a field that can be absent</summary>
<pre><code>data
  id?               string             Full tag ref name, for example refs/tags/v1.0.0.
  displayId?        string             Short tag name, for example v1.0.0.
  type?             TAG|ANNOTATED_TAG  TAG for a lightweight tag, ANNOTATED_TAG for one carrying its own object.
  latestCommit?     string             SHA1 of the commit the tag points at.
  latestChangeset?  string             SHA1 of the tagged changeset.
  hash?             string             SHA1 of the tag object itself.
</code></pre>
</details>

## `bb tag delete`

Delete repository tag

```text
bb tag delete <tag> [flags]
```

```bash
# Delete a tag; at a terminal bb asks first
bb tag delete v1.2.0 --repo PROJ/repo

# In a script, where nobody can be asked
bb tag delete v1.2.0 --repo PROJ/repo --yes
```

`-y, --yes`
:   Confirm without being asked; applies only when the target is named with --repo PROJECT/slug

Inherited from [`bb tag`](#bb-tag):

`--filter string`
:   Filter text for tag names

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Checks your permission and the current state this depends on, without changing anything (preconditions-checked)

<details class="note" data-search-exclude>
<summary>Output with <code>--json</code>, where <code>?</code> marks a field that can be absent</summary>
<pre><code>data
  status  string  Always ok when the command succeeds; a failure reports an error envelope instead.
  tag     string  Short name of the tag that was deleted.
</code></pre>
</details>

## `bb tag list`

List repository tags

```text
bb tag list [flags]
```

```bash
# A repository's tags
bb tag list --repo PROJ/repo

# The 1.x releases, most recently changed first
bb tag list --repo PROJ/repo --filter v1. --order-by MODIFICATION
```

`--all`
:   Return every result rather than the first --limit

`--limit int`
:   Maximum number of results to return (default 25)

`--order-by string`
:   Tag ordering (one of: ALPHABETICAL, MODIFICATION)

`--start int`
:   Start offset for list operations

Inherited from [`bb tag`](#bb-tag):

`--filter string`
:   Filter text for tag names

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Runs as usual: this command changes nothing, so there is nothing to hold back

## `bb tag view`

View repository tag

```text

```

```bash
# The commit a tag points at
```
